reading.title: Small Endings, Big Changes
reading.purpose: Find out how four word endings can help you read and build long words.
paras: A suffix is a word part added to the end of a word, and it can change the word's job. Learning a few suffixes helps you understand many new words. Four common endings are -ify, -ize, -ity, and -ence or -ance.

The endings -ify and -ize usually turn words into verbs that mean to make or to become. To simplify a recipe is to make it easier to follow. A water filter can purify a stream by removing dirt. A hand lens can magnify a seed so that it looks much bigger. A town may modernize its library by adding computers and new lights.

The ending -ity names a quality or condition. Popularity is the state of being liked by many people. Curiosity is a strong wish to learn something, and generosity is the habit of giving freely. Notice that each noun comes from an adjective: popular, curious, and generous.

The endings -ence and -ance also make nouns. Patience is the ability to wait calmly. Independence means freedom from the control of others, and importance tells how much something matters. When a word ends this way, you can often guess that it names an idea you cannot touch.
The next time you meet a long, unfamiliar word, look at its ending first. It may give you a clue about the job the word does.

qs.q: In paragraph 2, to "purify" a stream means to
choices: clean it by taking out dirt
make it flow faster by clearing away the rocks
make it look bigger so it is easier to see clearly
change it so that it fits new ideas and tools
qs.why: The text says a water filter can purify a stream "by removing dirt."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what popularity is?
choices: Curiosity is a strong wish to learn something, and generosity is the habit of giving freely.
The ending -ity names a quality or condition.
Popularity is the state of being liked by many people.
Notice that each noun comes from an adjective: popular, curious, and generous.
qs.why: This sentence gives the meaning of popularity directly.

ev.text: Popularity is the state of being liked by many people.

qs.q: Why might a town modernize its library?
choices: To remove dirt from all of the books and the shelves
To fit new tools such as computers and better lights
To make the rules for visitors easier for everyone to follow
To make the building look bigger when seen from far away
qs.why: Modernize means to change something to fit new ideas or tools, and the text gives computers and new lights as examples.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only verbs can ever end with a suffix in the English language.
Every long word is too hard for any student to read well.
A suffix always makes a word mean the opposite of its base word.
Word endings can give clues about a word's job and meaning.
qs.why: Each paragraph shows what an ending tells you, and the last one says to look at the ending first.

clues.text: to make it easier to follow
so that it looks much bigger
the state of being liked by many people
